newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A surprise jump in October trade data helped the bond market to a firmer close on Monday despite the fact that the rand weakened by more than three cents on the day and leading to suggestions that the data was leaked.
At the local close, the key R150 was quoted at a 15.81, off an intraday low of 15.79 percent and from 15.89 percent on Friday.

Dealers said the bond market initially looked set to move sideways on the day after strength on the U.S. bond market offset the negative effects of poor October money supply and private sector credit data released on Friday.
The release of October trade data at 1200 GMT, however, put paid to any prospects of a dull afternoon.

Latest South African Revenue Services data showed the country's trade surplus rocketed by 484.7 percent in October to a 3.9 billion surplus -- far exceeding economists' most optimistic forecast of a 1.2 billion rand surplus.
"It was a shocking figure...very bullish for the market," one trader said.
However, other traders said yields had begun to move well before the data was released, resulting in the market not strengthening as much as would have been expected.
"If you look at the price action before the figure came out...either someone has been lucky or they have been getting the figures before the rest of the market," one said.
"The market should have moved 10 or 15 points on this figure," he added.
South African Revenue Service officials were unavailable for comment on either the reason for the sharp increase in the surplus or the talk that the data was leaked.
Dealers who argued that the data had been leaked said the fact that the bond market had ignored the rand's sharp weakening backed their argument.
The rand weakened more than three cents on the day to 4.6385/6435 against the dollar from 4.6005/6055 on Friday, before easing further in after-hours trade to 4.6470/6520 at 1500 GMT.
Dealers said the currency had been pummelled on the day by a hefty import order which had left the market scrambling for dollars.
"The importers were in taking lots and lots of dollars out," a trader said.

Talk in the market was that the Reserve Bank had assisted the currency at its day's worst level of 4.65 against the dollar, while the release of the trade data "might have also capped it a little bit".

Dealers said the breach of 4.6250 to 4.6300 on the topside had been crucial and was now providing support for the dollar. They expected the currency to trade in a 4.62 to 4.65 range for the rest of the week.
Against the crosses, the rand was at 7.8222/8353 against sterling from 7.7317/7447 on Friday and at 0.3309/3314 marks from 0.3332/3337 marks previously.
On the money market, banks kept their three-month NCD rates unchanged at between 17.00 and 17.10 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was quoted in a 16.40 to 16.65 percent range.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 8.605 billion rand on Saturday from 9.923 billion rand on Friday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners bought a net 21.57 million rand worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 111.64 million rand on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 6.17 billion rand on Friday from 37.44 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
